$schema_note: Modeled workflow estimates for scripts/measure_skill_context.py. Each workflow is an explicit, hand-maintained file list checked against the SKILL.md/rules routing that existed at the time this file was last edited — it is not derived by following Markdown links or by crawling directories, and it does not by itself prove what a real session actually loads. Update it whenever a skill's routing changes. The script's own revision check only reports whether the current working tree differs from git HEAD (an uncommitted-change check) — it does not know when this file was last reconciled against routing, and cannot detect a routing change that was already committed cleanly, which would leave a workflow row stale with no signal from the script. The script does separately fail clearly, per workflow, when a listed file is missing or git-ignored.
excluded_external: Laravel Boost's laravel-best-practices, testing-best-practices, and inertia-vue-development skills — real cost when installed, not published in this repository, not measurable here.
The artifact-design skill that document-it/SKILL.md requires loading before writing any Artifact page — same caveat.
Application/project code, prior conversation history, and tool-call output (command results, diffs, search results) for every workflow.
excluded_project_docs: docs/skill-authoring-methodology.md and docs/skill-consumption.md serve a skill's author or a project's installer, not a running pipeline workflow — no SKILL.md or rule file in skills/ references either one.

workflows.name: review-it: standalone review
workflows.notes: All three rule files are consulted on essentially every invocation, in the order SKILL.md's own Rules list states.

workflows.name: lab-it: investigation-and-answer only
workflows.notes: rules/plan-synthesis.md loads only for the 'Plan feature architecture' workflow; a plain investigation-and-answer request never reaches it.

workflows.name: document-it: new Markdown guide, evidence already sufficient
workflows.notes: lab-it not routed to because evidence is already sufficient and current. SKILL.md's "Document existing architecture" trigger hands off to rules/authoring.md for the write/publish procedure.

workflows.name: document-it: new Artifact guide
workflows.notes: Same as the Markdown-guide row, plus the Artifact scaffold. The external artifact-design skill this requires is not counted (excluded_external).

workflows.name: document-it: reconcile existing Markdown guide, evidence routed through lab-it (cross-skill)
workflows.notes: SKILL.md's "Update an existing guide" trigger hands off to rules/authoring.md for locating the target and the situation handling; rules/authoring.md then points to rules/maintenance.md for the judgment calls, and rules/maintenance.md routes to rules/doc-style.md for how a connected change gets written. rules/template.html is not reached because this is a Markdown, not an Artifact, guide.

workflows.name: document-it: standalone review of a single Markdown guide
workflows.notes: Reviewing a published guide's completeness, independent of writing or updating it. Assumes current evidence and rules/review.md's checklist answer every question on their own, with no need to open an additional owning reference -- under that assumption, this loads only SKILL.md's activation/routing and rules/review.md's checklist, and does not execute rules/authoring.md's writing procedure. rules/review.md's own citations to SKILL.md's "Maintaining both formats" and to rules/maintenance.md for identity preservation are consulted only when a specific claim actually needs checking against them; a review consulting one of those owning references for one fact is not the same as executing its writing procedure, but if that consultation happens, add the consulted file to this row rather than treating the two-file total as a hard ceiling.

workflows.name: document-it: standalone review of a paired Markdown + Artifact guide
workflows.notes: Same assumption and file set as the single-Markdown-guide review row: rules/review.md carries one shared checklist for both formats, including the "Both formats maintained" synchronization and authorized-divergence checks, so reviewing a paired guide costs no additional file over reviewing one format alone, as long as current evidence and the checklist suffice without consulting further guidance.

workflows.name: plan-it: one resource/CRUD feature, UI in scope, single shape
workflows.notes: rules/capability-checklist.md, rules/plan-md-input.md, and rules/discovered-work.md are the unused alternates for this shape.

workflows.name: plan-it: same feature, mixed characteristics (secondary checklist)
workflows.notes: rules/feature-classification.md's own 'secondary questions' allowance adds rules/capability-checklist.md on top of the single-shape row.

workflows.name: implement-it: one ordinary issue, no stack companion, no activation changes, no isolation, no reconstruction (cross-skill review-it call before Gate 1)
workflows.notes: The ordinary path per implement-it/SKILL.md's current Rules list. No commit in this issue flips a configuration/feature-flag/environment-conditioned gate, so rules/activation-ordering.md is not loaded; isolation-verification.md, worktree-preservation.md, and commit-reconstruction.md are not loaded on this path either.

workflows.name: implement-it: same issue, activation-dependent commit ordering with its required isolation verification (no reconstruction)
workflows.notes: A commit being built flips a configuration/feature-flag/environment-conditioned gate, so verification.md's commit-building loop hands off to rules/activation-ordering.md for the reordering procedure; that same activation step is one of verification.md's own named examples for when an intermediate committed state needs isolation-verification proof, without a review correction folding into an already-committed, unpublished commit.

workflows.name: implement-it: same issue, unpublished-history reconstruction, no activation changes
workflows.notes: commit-reconstruction.md mandates isolation verification for every rebuilt commit (its own step 11). No commit in this issue flips an activation gate, so rules/activation-ordering.md is not loaded.

workflows.name: implement-it: ordinary issue composed with laravel-inertia-stack for one filtered-index task (cross-skill)
workflows.notes: blueprints/filters-and-sorting.md's own 'Testing' section routes further to rules/test-ownership.md and blueprints/pest-testing.md; its 'Naming and location' section cites rules/php-conventions.md for the abstract-base-class/final-subclass convention.

workflows.name: ship-it: PR readiness and authorized creation, local files only
workflows.notes: Local-file subtotal only. milestone-pr-readiness.md's own citation into milestone-completion.md's shared guidance is conditional (a manual-testing finding needing scope interpretation, or confirming Backlog eligibility) — see the 'broader estimate' row below for when that citation is actually followed.

workflows.name: ship-it: PR readiness, broader estimate (shared guidance actually consulted)
workflows.notes: Adds rules/milestone-completion.md when the pass actually follows milestone-pr-readiness.md's own citation into it.

workflows.name: ship-it: CI-failure investigation and correction handoff
workflows.notes: Step 3 of ci-failure-correction.md unconditionally directs consulting implement-it/rules/review-gates.md's 'when to stop and ask' standard, so that file is mandatory for this path, not merely conditional.

workflows.name: ship-it: full delivery happy path (readiness -> creation -> closure -> release, no CI failure)
workflows.notes: Already includes milestone-completion.md, so the PR-readiness row's own broader-estimate distinction does not add anything further here.
